data.title: F4 Uranium to raise up to C$1.5M via flow-through financing
data.description:
F4 Uranium Corp. (FFUCF) has announced a non-brokered private placement of up to 17.65M  flow-through (FT) common shares priced at C$0.085 per share, targeting gross proceeds of up to approximately C$1.5M.

Proceeds will fund eligible Canadian exploration and critical mineral mining expenditures across F4 Uranium's Athabasca Basin projects in Saskatchewan by December 31, 2027, with all qualifying expenditures renounced to subscribers effective December 31, 2026.

The offering is expected to close around December 18, 2026, subject to TSX-V approval, the offering includes a four-month-and-one-day hold period and potential insider participation exempt from formal valuation and minority shareholder approval.

data.title: Black Friday: Shoppers hunt for deals as investors buy staples
data.description:
Sticky inflation and affordability concerns aren't deterring Americans from going shopping this year, but they're definitely putting pressure on wallets and pocketbooks. An estimated 182.7M people across the country are planning to shop in-store and online from Thanksgiving Day through Cyber Monday, according to the National Retail Federation, which is 4M people less than the record high notched last year. To keep budgets in check, many are taking steps to manage holiday costs, including buying less expensive gifts or cutting back in other areas.

Snapshot: Black Friday continues to be the most popular day to shop, with around 69% (126M people) planning to take advantage of deals. The NRF even forecasts that total holiday spending during November and December will surpass $1T for the first time, with sales predicted to grow 4.2% over 2025. The numbers highlight the resilience of the American consumer, which continues to bolster the U.S. economy.

"Holiday shopping continues to be pulled forward, but Thanksgiving weekend remains an important shopping event for consumers," noted Allison Zeller, NRF Vice President of Industry and Consumer Insights. "Shoppers are looking for deals, and retailers are delivering great value on gifts while creating special experiences that keep the Thanksgiving weekend shopping tradition going."

Stock returns: The investing side of retail reflects the budget-conscious dynamic, with defensive essentials outpacing discretionary splurges. Consumer Staples (XLP) has been a clear sector winner, gaining 4.1% over the past month, 10.4% over six months, and 18.2% over the past year. Standout YTD performers include big-box stores like Target (TGT) +76%, Costco (COST) +26% and Walmart (WMT) +18%, as well as consumer giants like Coca-Cola (KO) +40%, Colgate-Palmolive (CL) +26% and Procter & Gamble (PG) +21%. While an AI pullback and tariff uncertainty have slashed high-valuation growth exposure, capital has steadily rotated into businesses prized for low cyclicality, durable cash flows, and dependable dividends. data.title: Rheinmetall trims long-term sales target as defense projects face delays
data.description:
• Germany's Rheinmetall (RNMBF) lowered its 2030 sales target to €33B-€37B from approximately €45B previously.
  • The defense group said it was adopting a more conservative planning approach following setbacks in several major projects.
  • The revised outlook comes after Germany cancelled the F126 frigate program, delays affected advance payments for the Arminius Boxer armored vehicle program, and ammunition approval bottlenecks constrained business development.
  • The F126 cancellation also prompted Rheinmetall (RNMBF) to lower its 2030 sales expectations for its naval division to €3.5B-€4B from its earlier €5B target.
  • Separately, Rheinmetall (RNMBF) announced an order worth ~€738M to supply Romania with an additional 66 Lynx armored vehicles.

data.title: Nvidia gains premarket as stock heads for end to volatile week
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) shares rose 4% before the opening bell of a shortened trading session Friday. But the gains are offering little evidence that the chipmaker had put a volatile week behind it.

The stock has swung sharply over the past three sessions, surging 31% on Monday after Jensen Huang's dramatic return as chief executive and president, only to give back some of those gains in the following sessions.

Nvidia fell 5.9% on Tuesday as investors took profits. Trading remained choppy ahead of the Thanksgiving break, with shares closing 3.91% lower on Wednesday after falling as much as 7% during the session.

The AI trade, with Nvidia at its center, has faced pressure from concerns over whether massive investments in AI will generate sufficient returns, a possible slowdown in spending after the U.S. midterm elections, and rising interest rates. Huang's departure had added another layer of uncertainty. 

His return has removed that concern, at least for now. Huang's comeback added about $1T to Nvidia's market value and lifted the broader AI trade. But this has also introduced a key man risk in the company.

data.title: IKEA is rolling out more smaller stores
data.description:
IKEA is becoming a competitive threat to online home furnishings and decor companies in a new way by actively shifting its U.S. strategy away from relying solely on massive, isolated suburban big blue box warehouses toward a dense, accessible omnichannel network. Notably, the Sweden-based company is making a sizable $2.2B investment to prioritize convenience, speed, and proximity to city dwellers.

The initiative, which is a reaction to changing post-pandemic shopping habits and declining foot traffic at distant suburban warehouses, includes aggressively rolling out smaller, urban-friendly footprints. New small-format stores near high-traffic city centers are roughly one-tenth the size of traditional IKEA warehouses. The stores feature a curated assortment of cash-and-carry home accessories alongside interior design planning services. Recent urban pushes include Culver City, Manhattan's SoHo neighborhood, and expansion into metro hubs across Texas, Illinois, and Colorado.

In the U.S. home furnishings and decor market, IKEA primarily competes with online-first giants like Wayfair and Amazon, big-box retailers such as Target, Walmart, Home Depot, and Lowe's, and specialty home chains including Crate & Barrel, CB2, West Elm (WSM), Pottery Barn (WSM), Ashley HomeStore, At Home, and HomeGoods (TJX).

data.title: Hackers reportedly breach US Air Force Cloud One system
data.description:
• Hackers have reportedly breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data.
  • The intrusion at Cloud One was ‌discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system, sources told Reuters, adding that the discovery has led to disruption across the platform. 
  • In a statement to Reuters, the Air Force said it "does not comment on the ​security posture, vulnerabilities or operational status of specific networks and systems. We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems ​and mission capabilities."
  • Initiated in 2017, Cloud One was meant to serve as a one-stop shop for the Air Force's ⁠IT needs, combining the resources of four operators — Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), Oracle (ORCL) and Alphabet  (GOOG) (GOOGL) — to power scores of applications including ones that manage personnel data and pay ​or logistics and maintenance.
  • SAIC (SAIC) was the prime contractor for Cloud One until 2025, when Leidos (LDOS) took over. Cloud One is among the US military's biggest cloud platforms, sources said. "A breach here is a big deal, the report added. Investigators have called in Cyber Command, the US military's cyber force, to assess the damage.
  • The discovery of the hack has reportedly led to a range of disruption. The report also said that efforts to migrate back-office applications to Cloud One, a longstanding military priority, have been paused. Updates to applications already running on Cloud One were blocked, leaving Air Force personnel unable to apply fixes just as a new batch of serious software vulnerabilities has been disclosed across the technology industry. According to one source some users had their administrator rights revoked.

data.title: AM Markets Need to Know: Trump disputes GDP, OPEC pressure, and more
data.description:
Stock index futures surged on Friday as Wall Street looked to close out a volatile week with a winning session, while Treasury yields moved higher following the Thanksgiving holiday break.

Here are the five news items investors should watch:

Trump challenges revised GDP figures: President Donald Trump called for an immediate investigation into the Commerce Department's revised third-quarter GDP figures, alleging that officials deliberately released inaccurate data ahead of the November midterm elections. The department revised annualized economic growth to 4.3% from its initial estimate of 3.4%. Trump described the revision as a "record setting error" but provided no evidence of deliberate manipulation.

U.S. pressured Venezuela and Iraq over OPEC: The Trump administration encouraged Venezuela and Iraq to consider leaving OPEC and blocked Venezuela from paying its annual membership dues, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The pressure targeted two of the cartel's five founding members as Washington sought to encourage greater oil production. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman subsequently intervened to persuade the administration to drop its push against Venezuela.

Trump defends Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return: President Donald Trump said Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang was happy to return to his position, describing the executive's reinstatement as a "second term." Speaking at Mar-a-Lago, Trump defended his intervention despite bipartisan national security concerns. He offered no specific details when asked about the information supporting his confidence in Huang.

School districts push Google to disable AI features: Los Angeles Unified School District has disabled Google's (GOOG) (GOOGL) AI-generated search summaries on school-issued devices, as districts demand permanent opt-out options for educational products. The move makes LAUSD, which serves approximately 500,000 students, the largest district to sideline the feature. The dispute could put pressure on Google's position in the U.S. education market.

Icahn Enterprises faces mounting refinancing pressure: Icahn Enterprises (IEP) faces growing debt concerns after warning that it may not be able to refinance $1.4B of bonds due in May on acceptable terms, or at all. Yields on the bonds have climbed above 14% from ~ 6% three months ago, while some 2029 notes have reportedly topped 30%. Its major holding, CVR Energy (CVI), has also lost approximately 46% since agreeing to acquire two refineries.
